transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (FjordWorks Head of Platform), Jonas (CTO), Samir (Lead ML), Elena (Security)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on integration approach; customer wants a pilot to test latency and observability; security and data residency are gating items.

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is the onramp integration handoff, um, quick intros then we'll jump into the architecture and what FjordWorks is trying to do
[00:12] Maya: hi all, thanks. i'm Maya, head of platform at FjordWorks. we run a multi-tenant analytics platform, lots of vector search + embeddings today, experimenting with LLM features for customer facing assistants
[00:22] Jonas: Jonas here, CTO. our main asks: predictable latency for query paths, cost control, and strict EU data residency for PII workloads
[00:30] Diego: great, thanks. super helpful. quick question, are you prototyping with LangChain or LlamaIndex or both?
[00:36] Samir: primarily LangChain right now, with a few LlamaIndex experiments for document stores. our retriever->rerank->generate pipeline is in place but the production serving is the pain point
[00:49] Priya: ok, and roughly what are your p50/p95 targets and tokens per request?
[00:53] Samir: target p50 is under 120ms for short prompts (~200 tokens), p95 under 450ms. request volume is small but bursty — maybe 30 req/s sustained per region, spikes to 200 for special events
[01:12] Avery: good, that's the kind of signal we need for sizing Dedicated or evaluating Hosted with burst capacity. quick high level: Redwood Hosted gives fastest onboarding and streaming. Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and predictable throughput. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulated flows — Elena i'll flag you for the security part
[01:31] Elena: yeah, data residency + KMS are must-haves. we also need SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs for the pilot. how does Redwood handle KMS?
[01:40] Diego: we support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted has managed encryption but we can integrate with customer KMS via an enterprise plan — there was a small doc, i'll share. note: sometimes the doc references HSM in our private package, it's labeled HSM but it's really KMS-backed HSM integration
[02:03] Jonas: ok, and what about connector support? we want to keep LangChain in place and not rewrite stacks
[02:09] Priya: Redwood SDKs are LangChain-friendly — we have examples for the Python SDK using chains and retrievers, and we maintain a lightweight LlamaIndex adapter. i'll drop the repo links after. the common pattern is: app -> gateway/proxy (sidecar or central) -> Redwood API or Dedicated endpoint.
[02:30] Maya: gateway/proxy — we'd prefer a sidecar for multi-tenant routing, but worried about additional latency
[02:36] Diego: sidecar can add a few ms but gives better tenant isolation and local rate limiting. central proxy reduces duplication but can be a single point unless autoscaled. both work — we usually recommend a hybrid: sidecar for per-tenant quotas + a central egress gateway for aggregation and observability hooks
[02:54] Samir: what are the rate limiting primitives? per-tenant tokens, concurrent request caps? how do quotas map to Dedicated pools?
[03:02] Priya: we expose per-API key rate limits and quotas, token-based billing. For Dedicated you can map virtual pools and route heavy tenants to reserved capacity to avoid noisy neighbor issues. quotas are configurable: request/s, tokens/day, and burst windows
[03:22] Jonas: we need enforcement at the gateway so a malicious customer can't exceed quota and blow budgets
[03:27] Diego: yep, enforce at the proxy/sidecar layer with JWT claims tied to tenant IDs. we also surface throttling events in the Console and emit webhooks/metrics for downstream billing integration
[03:41] Maya: observability: we need per-call traces, token-level cost, and prompt-level metadata (which retriever used, rerank score) — can you surface that?
[03:51] Priya: yes, Redwood Console provides token cost breakdown, per-route latency, and you can attach arbitrary metadata tags to requests. we also have tracing hooks for open telemetry; the SDK emits spans you can correlate with your traces
[04:08] Samir: how accurate is the token cost? we need it to reconcile with our billing quickly
[04:13] Diego: token accounting is deterministic on our runtime; small diffs maybe in streaming partial tokens but overall it's consistent. we export token manifests and raw usage logs for reconciliation
[04:28] Maya: about LlamaIndex — will existing indices break or do we need a transformation?
[04:34] Priya: should be minimal. LlamaIndex serializes doc stores; our LlamaIndex adapter handles retriever calls and streaming responses. if you use embedded KV caches on your side, we can integrate caching hints to reduce calls to the model
[04:50] Jonas: caching hints? explain
[04:52] Diego: e.g., prefix caching for repeated prompts or KV cache for completion contexts. Redwood runtime supports KV cache for autoregressive sessions which cuts cost for multi-turn chat style interactions
[05:06] Samir: nice. on the Dedicated sizing — how do we pick instance types and how dynamic is autoscaling?
[05:12] Priya: Dedicated supports GPU pools with configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. pickup uses a policy based on inflight requests and queue latencies. we typically start with an estimate and run a short load test to calibrate. we'll provide a recommended baseline based on your p50/p95 and token mix
[05:32] Maya: for the pilot we'd prefer Hosted because it's fastest to get going, but we need to validate observability and data residency — is that possible?
[05:40] Diego: yes, Hosted can be used for non-PII workloads and we can spin up a region in EU for data locality. For PII you likely need Dedicated or Private so keys never leave your VPC. we can do a hybrid pilot: non-PII on Hosted EU region and a dedicated private flow for PII tests
[05:58] Jonas: timeline — can we do a two-week pilot? we want a realistic workload replay and benchmarks for latency & cost
[06:04] Avery: two-week pilot is doable. action: we'll provision sandbox project and sample keys; you'll provide prompt set and traffic profile; Diego will run bench to capture p50/p95 and token cost.
[06:15] Elena: on compliance: audit logs and SSO are needed. do you have prebuilt SAML integrations?
[06:20] Priya: yes SAML/Okta integration is standard for Console access. audit logs are available in Private and Dedicated with more retention options as an add-on for Hosted enterprise tiers
[06:34] Samir: one concern: our app does synchronous calls during page load, we can't have 300-500ms p95 — any patterns to keep latency low?
[06:43] Diego: for synchronous short queries, we recommend using smaller models, prompt engineering to reduce tokens, and prefix caching. Another pattern is to materialize likely answers to a fast cache and fallback to live model only if cache miss. Also keep an eye on batching — batching improves throughput but hurts tail latency, so don't enable aggressive batching on latency-critical routes
[07:09] Maya: ok, tradeoff noted. about the gateway: do you recommend sidecar as a library or a separate proxy? we have a mix of serverless and k8s services
[07:18] Priya: for serverless, a central egress proxy is easier. for k8s, a sidecar works well. you can also run an envoy filter with Lua to inject per-tenant headers; our SDK is lightweight so embedding logic in a sidecar or small library both fine. we have examples for lambda + API gateway as well
[07:40] Jonas: any gotchas with streaming and function calling when going through a proxy?
[07:44] Diego: proxies need to support streaming webhooks and keepalive; if you terminate the connection you'll break partial streams. we recommend proxying raw websocket or using chunked transfer-encoding passthrough for streaming. function calling meta needs to be preserved as well, so attach the function schema in metadata headers
[08:05] Samir: we use OpenTelemetry already — does Redwood integrate traces automatically?
[08:09] Priya: yes, we have tracing hooks and our SDK emits spans. you can map to your trace-id via a header and correlate. we also push logs/metrics to your ingest if you want or provide export to common sinks (Datadog, Prometheus, S3)
[08:27] Maya: billing visibility — do you give line-item token usage per tenant?
[08:31] Diego: yes, Console has per-API key breakdown with token counts, model used, and cost estimate. for Dedicated we also provide token attribution per pool and per route if you push route tags in requests
[08:44] Jonas: curious about fallbacks — do you have automatic fallback to cheaper models if capacity is constrained?
[08:50] Priya: we support routing policies. you can set a priority list: prefer high-quality instance, fallback to quantized or smaller models, or route to another region. fallbacks are seamless and we record them in logs so you can analyze quality impact
[09:06] Samir: quality monitoring — can we tie regressions to prompt sets?
[09:11] Diego: yes Redwood Optimize integrates evals tied to prompt sets and will alert if outputs degrade. it can also suggest quantization or model changes per workload. we'll demo that in the follow-up
[09:25] Maya: okay, practical: what's required for us to start the pilot?
[09:29] Avery: three things: 1) sample prompts/traffic profile 2) security checklist sign-off for EU Hosted sandbox or Dedicated baseline 3) access to a small set of production-like data for replay in sandbox
[09:43] Maya: we can do that. Samir will put together a 48-hour sample and a 2-week traffic replay.
[09:49] Jonas: and for success criteria, we'll measure p50/p95, token cost per request, and no data leakage.
[09:57] Elena: adding security: encryption at rest, KMS controls, and audit trails must be validated during pilot
[10:05] Diego: understood. i'll attach our SOC2 extracts and KMS integration notes. FYI sometimes the SOC doc references older product names in it — but the content is valid — i'll clarify in the email
[10:19] Priya: Diego, also remind them about gateway examples for sidecar vs central with code snippets
[10:25] Diego: will do.
[10:28] Samir: one more — we rely on vector DB with LangChain retriever. any advice for reducing calls to model for retrieval latency?
[10:35] Priya: use batch retrieval and prefetching, reduce candidate set, and use a lightweight reranker or dense-sparse cascade. Redwood can run the rerank step in the same call to the model to reduce round trips if you colocate retriever and model calls in the same request path
[10:52] Maya: ok that's useful.
[10:55] Avery: quick recap before we close: Redwood to send SOC2/KMS notes, SDK/LangChain examples, provision sandbox keys; FjordWorks to provide prompt set, traffic replay, and confirm EU data residency. We schedule the technical deep dive to focus on gateway proxy patterns and a Dedicated sizing consult.
[11:16] Jonas: sounds good. can we do the technical deep dive next week?
[11:20] Avery: yes, i'll send a calendar invite — Diego and Priya will lead.
[11:24] Elena: for next steps please cc security mailbox and include retention numbers for audit logs
[11:30] Diego: noted. we'll include retention tiers and export options.
[11:36] Samir: small nit: do you have any sample latency/cost spreadsheet we can use to model our pricing?
[11:41] Priya: yes a benchmarking template, i'll attach it. it has example token mixes and model decode rates.
[11:48] Maya: great. thanks everyone.
[11:50] Avery: thanks all, we'll follow up with deliverables. end.
